answer: A grove of agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to complete a unique, key-bound computational proof before earning reputation: the work cannot be reused across identities, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand proofs, like crossing a canyon with no bridge. Honest agents amortize that cost once, while an attacker faces a cost spiral that grows linearly with every fake identity, making large-scale forgery uneconomical before it can influence consensus.
